key_insight: V-PaSS improves perovskite solar-cell prediction by encoding absorber composition and device stack with physics-aware, chemically meaningful representations that can extrapolate to new alloys and architectures.
engineering_relevance: The approach can help researchers screen unexplored perovskite device designs more reliably, especially when experimental data come from unfamiliar labs or previously unseen material combinations.
method: Interpolates mixed-cation and mixed-halide absorber structures from 23 pure ABX3 endpoint crystal graphs using Vegard’s law plus learned bandgap bowing.
Represents device stacks with layer order, cell polarity, interfacial band offsets, and scientific-language-model embeddings of chemical descriptions.
Uses a physics-aware semantic architecture that supports extrapolative prediction beyond standard categorical or fixed crystal-graph encodings.
evidence_signal: Under an institution-grouped evaluation with unseen laboratories in test data, V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE, outperforming 14 tested models and improving over a gradient-boosted baseline by 5.2% relative error reduction.
watch_item: The method depends on physically valid endpoint structures and learned interpolation assumptions, so performance may be less reliable for chemistries far outside the available 23-compound alloy space.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
